incident-bot: Paging: anomalous session spike detected from edge cluster ap-southeast-1 — 5xx rate up 4x, p50 latency up 2x, many short-lived sessions. auto-threshold triggered at 23:04 UTC. paging maya (SRE oncall).

maya (SRE oncall): seeing huge session fanout from ~120K unique IPs, most hitting /v1/embeddings/batch and /chat/stream. looks like a scraping farm.

zach (infra): charts look like coordinated bursts every ~30s. backend pools saturating; queues backpressure -> 503s.

kevin (edge): WAF signatures picking up some known botnet UA patterns but majority are low-entropy UAs, rotating IPs via proxies. need to avoid collateral on legit traffic.

maya (SRE oncall): plan: 1) short-term: shape traffic at edge + throttle embeddings batch endpoint 2) medium: tighten WAF fingerprint rules 3) notify support for customer-impact assessment. executing live now.

ops-bot: Executing runbook step 1: apply traffic-shaper in region ap-southeast-1. Command: `edgectl traffic-shape --region ap-southeast-1 --policy session-storm-2026 --concurrency 1500 --burst 5000`

zach (infra): applied shaping policy. seeing drop in connection churn, but embeddings queue still heavy — batch endpoint still accepting large payloads.

maya (SRE oncall): temporary kill switch for batch embeddings: set feature toggle EMBEDDINGS_BATCH_ENABLED=false for the region. will fail fast to per-item embeddings API which is rate-limited.

kevin (edge): toggled EMBEDDINGS_BATCH_ENABLED=false via config-service. propagation ~30s. adding a 10s 429 ramp for any residual batch requests to avoid retries piling up.

emily (support): some customers are already posting in support. which orgs affected and what msg should we send?

lia (product): quick triage: high-throughput customers using batch embeddings and some internal QA jobs. no degradation for chat-gen endpoints except slight latency increase for heavy sessions. recommend customer notice to affected customers explaining temporary batch disable for stability and ETA for re-enable.

maya (SRE oncall): customer impact summary for support: "We temporarily disabled batched embeddings in ap-southeast-1 due to abusive traffic patterns causing degraded performance. Single-item embeddings continue to work (rate-limited). We're shaping traffic and tuning WAF; we expect to re-enable batches after verification (approx 1-2 hours)."

emily (support): copying that to support template. sending proactive alerts to top-10 high-throughput customers now.

zach (infra): next: WAF tuning. I propose fingerprint rule: block header combos with UA matching /python-requests.*(gzip|curl)/ and high connection churn >20s with no JS. Also add rate cap per-IP and per-CIDR for new sessions.

kevin (edge): implemented adaptive WAF rule set wf-2367 with soft-block (challenge) for first 3 requests, then hard-block if challenge fails. rolling to ap-southeast-1 now. snippet: ```waf_rule {
  id: "wf-2367"
  action: "challenge_then_block"
  match: ["ua_regex:python-requests", "conn_churn>20", "no_js_header:true"]
  thresholds: { requests: 3, window_sec: 60 }
}```

maya (SRE oncall): good. also reduced default per-account embedding quota from 10k/min -> 2k/min in region for everyone temporarily to prevent abuse of burst credits. command: `quotactl update --region ap-southeast-1 --resource embeddings --limit 2000m`

ops-bot: Quota change applied.

zach (infra): monitoring dashboards: server error rate dropping, p95 latency improving. sessions still high but more controlled.

maya (SRE oncall): open questions: do we want to migrate traffic for top customers to another region or Dedicated? Lia?

lia (product): for customers on Dedicated, we can recommend moving heavy batch jobs to Dedicated pools. for self-serve, recommend retry/backoff guidance and switching to per-item embeddings. lia: will draft a short guidance doc and share link.

emily (support): sent notices to 7 customers; 3 acknowledged, 2 asked for ETA and mitigation plan, 2 reported no impact (good).

maya (SRE oncall): root cause hypothesis: large distributed scrape targeting embeddings batch to maximize tokens per request -> intentionally overwhelming KV cache + batch scheduler. attacker rotates IPs & UAs. mitigation summary so far: traffic shaping at edge, temporary embeddings-batch disable, adaptive WAF challenge rules, per-account quota reductions.

kevin (edge): also added a temporary header-based allowlist for verified partners (X-Partner-Key) so we don't impact partners. we used `edgectl header-allow add --key X-Partner-Key --values <redacted>`

zach (infra): next steps: 1) keep shaping and WAF on for 1-2 hours 2) run analysis to fingerprint botfarm IP ranges and push to ACL 3) rehearse enabling batches on canary with strict rate caps 4) write post-incident doc.

maya (SRE oncall): handoff: I'm on primary until 23:45 UTC. after that handoff to next oncall (zach). leaving checklist in runbook.

ops-bot: Handoff recorded: incident-2367890123, primary maya -> secondary zach at 23:45 UTC.

emily (support): any change to billing or quotas we should log for customers? lia?

lia (product): we won't bill extra or alter committed quotas; just temporary constraint. include note in outbound message.

maya (SRE oncall): closing note: don't add broad IP blocks yet, use behavioral/JS challenges where possible to reduce false positives. will start IP fingerprinting job now and share findings in this thread.

kevin (edge): thanks. initial IP fingerprint set attached: `ipset create storm-2367 hash:net` + ~18 subnets added. pushing to ACL gradually.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress — partial service restrictions active. Severity: high. Updates in this thread.

maya (SRE oncall): thanks team. scheduling a 30m blameless postmortem tomorrow 09:00 UTC. leave any telemetry links here.

zach (infra): telemetry: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/apac/session-storm-2367, logs: `s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2367890123/`

emily (support): support playbook link: https://docs.redwood.ai/support/incident-communication-template

maya (SRE oncall): last update before handoff: traffic shaping holding; WAF challenge effective; batch embeddings remain off regionally; customer notices sent. handing off to zach at 23:45 UTC.

zach (infra): taking over. will watch for false positives and prepare canary re-enable if traffic stays calm.

ops-bot: Thread closed by maya (SRE oncall) at 23:45 UTC.
